title: The Key: three persona builds, one exam
intro: Each of the nine actors gets three different persona cards. The cards are built from the same dated record. They are then given the same exam: predict what the actor actually did next, choosing only from actions the actor has really taken. Whichever card wins tells us where a persona's power comes from - the raw facts, the patterns in them, or what they imply.

tests.name: Test 1 - The Plain Record
tests.one_line: The agent sees the actor's history word for word: every dated, sourced fact in order, with a one-line identity at the top. Nothing else.
tests.built_from: The dated rows already on actor-persona.pages.dev, plus a new computed menu of the verbs the actor has actually used.
tests.bet: The record itself is the persona. Anything fancier has to beat this card to justify itself.
tests.exam: Pick the verb (and its direction) for each hidden later action. Scored by exact match against the real action.

tests.name: Test 2 - The Rule Card
tests.one_line: Instead of every fact, the agent gets a short list of patterns pulled from those facts: when X happened, this actor did Y, by about this much, within this many days.
tests.built_from: Trigger-to-response pairs computed from the dated rows and shared event list, following the site's own protocols (a trigger must be a dated row; gaps are computed, never guessed; three or more episodes make a rule). Sizes come from the record or from cited background research.
tests.bet: A few measured patterns beat a pile of facts, because patterns generalize and facts only describe.
tests.exam: Same hidden actions as Test 1. A rule fires when its trigger occurs in the question; the prediction is the rule's verb. Rules must beat 'nothing happens' and 'always the most common action'.

tests.name: Test 3 - The Expert Read
tests.one_line: The plain record plus four short readings of it, written once: what a psychologist, an economist, a political scientist, and a domain expert would notice.
tests.built_from: The four readings are written from the pre-cutoff rows only. Every claim uses action words and cites the row it rests on. At question time only the matching reading is attached.
tests.bet: The record says more than it states outright - trained eyes can pull out what it implies.
tests.exam: Same hidden actions. Only difference from Test 1 is the added lens, so any score gap belongs to the lens.

structure.what: One line: the actor's name and what kind of actor it is.
Every fact with its date, its verb, its wording, and a link to its source, in chronological order.
The verbs this actor has actually used, split into core (used twice or more) and rare (used once). The agent may answer only from this menu.
structure.origin: NEW - the site defines verbs ruled out, but not a per-actor menu of verbs observed

structure.what: Trigger, response, delay (median and range in days), size where the record quantifies it, direction (open or closed), and a stability check.
structure.origin: Partly - the site's reactions step has trigger/response and computed gaps; we add size, direction, stability, and status tiers

structure.what: Psychologist, economist, political scientist, domain expert - each a short reading of the record, every claim citing rows.
structure.origin: NEW - nothing like it in the schema

structure.what: Each topic maps to the one expert reading that answers it, so only that reading is attached per question.
structure.origin: NEW - reuses the site's topic taxonomy

structure.what: The actor's actions dated after its cutoff - each one is an exam question with a known answer (the verb).
structure.origin: NEW - the site stops at the cutoff; we keep the after-cutoff rows as the answer key

structure.what: The site's analyst-written sections: what the persona is for, who can stop the actor, what it can and cannot do, who follows its acts, what we don't know.
structure.origin: Yes - deliberately EXCLUDED from all three prompts so the tests measure the record, not analyst prose

changes.what: Added the observed action menu (core/rare verbs per actor)
changes.why: The exam needs the agent to choose from actions the actor has really taken. The site rules verbs out by power; nothing listed what each actor has actually done.

changes.what: Kept after-cutoff rows as a hidden answer key
changes.why: The site treats the cutoff as the end of the data. For backtesting, everything after it is the exam - so we split instead of dropping.

changes.what: Added size, direction, and leave-one-out stability to rules
changes.why: A rule with only a delay answers 'when', not 'how much' or 'which way'. Stability keeps rules whose direction survives having any single episode removed.

changes.what: Generated rules for the five actors that had none
changes.why: DeepSeek, Huawei, Jensen Huang, MIIT and SAMR had zero rules on the site; Test 2 needs cards for every actor.

changes.what: Added the four expert readings and the topic-to-lens routing
changes.why: Test 3's lens layer did not exist in the schema. It is generated once from pre-cutoff rows, with claims cited to row ids, and never updated by simulation output.

changes.what: Excluded all analyst-written sections from every prompt
changes.why: The three tests compare ways of turning a record into a persona. Purpose, standing, gates and short answers are analyst prose - leaving them in would contaminate all three arms equally but blur what's being tested.
One fixed prompt format per test, identical across actors, so score differences belong to the card, not the formatting.

changes.what: Rebuilt every rule card's statistics from pre-cutoff episodes only
changes.why: The fact-check found that 41 of the original 167 episodes used response rows from the actors' own hidden answer key - the card would have been trained on the exam. Post-cutoff episodes are kept for transparency under each rule but no longer count toward delays, sizes, or status. Two rules built entirely after the cutoff were excluded from the exam.

exam: Freeze the clock: each card is built only from facts dated before that actor's cutoff - for rule cards, enforced by dropping every episode whose response falls after the cutoff.
One question per hidden action: the agent is told the date and situation, then must pick one verb from its own menu plus a direction.
Scoring is mechanical: exact verb match (strict) and direction match (lenient), normalized by each actor's own consistency over time.
Two baselines run beside the three cards: predict nothing (the did-nothing base rate) and always pick the actor's most common verb.
Nothing any simulation produces is ever written back into a persona or the record.
footer: Built from the public data at actor-persona.pages.dev (9 actors, 7-step persona build). This site adds the test layers; it does not change the source records.
